objective: Redesign the release plan page without changing its existing business functions.

requirements.statement: Use a narrow plan directory and wide detail workspace on desktop.
acceptance: At desktop width >=1280, directory is narrower than detail; selected plan name, code, version and status are visible.
counterexample: List occupies the majority of page width.

requirements.statement: Retain two distinct normal and rollback sequence entries.
acceptance: Both entries show names and sequence/command counts and open the matching drawer.
counterexample: Both entries open the same sequence group.

requirements.statement: Retain horizontal P1/P2 sequences with multiple commands and all existing maintenance controls in drawers.
acceptance: Sequence and command add/edit/delete controls remain available with existing handlers; no date timeline appears.
counterexample: A sequence can display only one command.

requirements.statement: Provide readable responsive layouts with local sequence scrolling.
acceptance: At 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932, there is no page-level horizontal overflow; drawer controls are reachable in both themes.
counterexample: Toolbar overlaps the sequence title or the whole page scrolls sideways.

requirements.statement: Preserve project isolation, forms, permissions, cancellation and all existing asynchronous states.
acceptance: API payloads and handlers remain unchanged; cancelling deletion shows no failure and sends no deletion request; switching projects clears previous project content.
counterexample: Styling changes expose write controls to read-only users.

invariants: API, DTOs, projectId, rowVersion and permission checks unchanged
Preserve existing menu rename worktree changes
constraints: Only change the authorized Vue component and own task documents
Reuse semantic theme tokens and shared UI
No commit, push, branch switch or dependency changes
non_goals: Statistics blocks, introductory copy, new filters or date timeline

selected_approach.name: Compact directory and wide detail
selected_approach.reason: Preserves context when switching plans and entering sequence maintenance.

alternatives.name: Full list then separate detail page
alternatives.rejected_because: Adds navigation steps and changes current browsing workflow.

components.name: ReleaseDrillPlanView
components.responsibility: Plan directory, detail and existing maintenance overlays

interfaces.name: Existing release API functions
interfaces.contract: Preserve all parameters, DTOs, project scoping and optimistic locking.

data_flows.input: projectId prop and list API results
transitions: Use existing maintenance dialogs and handlers
data_flows.output: Current plan detail and sequence commands

error_handling.behavior: Keep existing error or forbidden result
error_handling.recovery: Existing reload action or administrator permission grant

error_handling.behavior: Retain current error feedback and cancel/close suppression
error_handling.recovery: Retry with existing form or return to unchanged selection

compatibility: Scoped styles, existing Vue and Element Plus components
operations: Frontend-only local verification, no backend restart

verification_strategy.signal: Build passes and specified browser journeys retain correct context without overlap
verification_strategy.method: Diff review, Vue build and desktop/mobile browser checks; report untested cases explicitly

assumptions.text: Existing local test services and session can be used for browser checks

decisions.decision: Use single-page split layout and existing drawers
decisions.reason: More room for details without altering behavior

risks.risk: Global styles or teleported overlays interfere with local layout
risks.mitigation: Distinct scoped classes and multi-viewport browser checks
